experience.description:
As a Research Assistant in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Hajee Mohammad Danesh Science and Technology University (HSTU) and Rajshahi University of Engineering Technology (RUET), I have worked under the mentorship of Md. Rasel Ahmed on multidisciplinary research spanning combustion engineering, hybrid renewable energy systems, and solar photovoltaic technologies. My work combines high-fidelity numerical simulation with techno-economic and environmental analysis to support cleaner, more efficient energy systems for Bangladesh and similar developing regions.

I contributed to a 3-dimensional CFD study using CONVERGE 3.0 and the SAGE detailed-chemistry combustion solver to compare the in-cylinder performance and emissions of hydrogen against gasoline, methane, and M10 in a port-fuel-injected spark-ignition engine, identifying operating conditions that maximize thermal efficiency while minimizing pollutant formation. I also worked on a HOMER Pro-based techno-economic and environmental optimization of six advanced hybrid renewable energy configurations- combining wind, solar PV, biogas, diesel, battery storage, and green-hydrogen electrolysis- for off-grid coastal electrification, supported by Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis and NSGA-II multi-objective optimization. In a related study, I helped benchmark PVsyst, HOMER Pro, and RETScreen for a standalone solar PV system, comparing their technical, financial, and emissions outputs to identify the most reliable design approach for off-grid island communities.

These projects have been published in peer-reviewed journals, including Next Energy, Energy Conversion and Management: X, and Discover Electronics. Building on this foundation, I am now extending my research into next-generation photovoltaics- designing and numerically simulating a lead-free, double-absorber perovskite solar cell optimized electron transport layers, aimed at improving power conversion efficiency while addressing the toxicity concerns of conventional lead-based perovskites.

education.synopsis: This dissertation presents the exciting frontier of hydrogen as a clean, high-efficiency fuel in spark-ignition engines, using advanced Converge CFD simulations to compare it against conventional fuels like gasoline, methane, and M10. Through a series of simulated combustion trials, hydrogen proves itself not just as a viable alternative but a standout performer-delivering smoother cylinder pressures, higher thermal efficiency, and near-zero emissions at optimal conditions. Particularly at an equivalence ratio of 0.4 and 3000 rpm, hydrogen showcases its potential to power the future of transportation with minimal environmental impact. The research boldly positions hydrogen as a clean-energy champion ready to replace carbon-heavy fuels in a world urgently seeking sustainability.

aboutText: Hi! I'm Rashedul Islam, a mechanical engineer a native of Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, with a strong and lasting interest in Computational Fluid Dynamics and hydrogen combustion. I completed my B.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering at Hajee Mohammad Danesh Science and Technology University (HSTU), Dinajpur, and from early on I found myself pulled toward the questions CFD lets you ask- how fuels ignite and burn, how flows behave under pressure and turbulence, and how small changes in geometry or chemistry ripple through a system's performance. That curiosity has stayed with me, and I continue to work with tools like CONVERGE, and COMSOL Multiphysics to explore combustion and reacting-flow problems, with hydrogen as a fuel of particular interest given its promise for cleaner energy systems.

Beyond CFD, I've been increasingly drawn into materials science and heat transfer. I'm fascinated by how materials behave under mechanical, thermal, and structural stress at the molecular level, and by the engineering challenge of moving heat efficiently through complex systems- both feel like natural extensions of the same simulation-driven mindset I bring to combustion work.

Renewable energy rounds out my interests. Having grown up in a coastal region shaped by resource constraints and grid instability, I care about hybrid and off-grid power systems- solar, wind, and biogas, and how they can be modeled, optimized, and deployed in places that need them most.

At the core of all this is a simple motivation: using computation to make sense of complex physical problems, and building engineering judgment that translates cleanly from simulation to the real world. I hope to keep deepening that work across CFD, materials science, heat transfer, and renewable energy in the years ahead.
profile.researchInterestText: My work centers on computational fluid dynamics and hydrogen combustion, extending into materials science, heat transfer, and additive manufacturing. Renewable energy systems- particularly hybrid, off-grid optimized solutions- round out this focus, with simulation-driven modeling as the common thread across all of it.
